title: Brightwell–Felsner–Trotter's cross-product conjecture for posets
statement:
Let $P=(X,\prec)$ be a finite poset, let $x,y,z\in X$ be distinct, and for integers $k,\ell$ let $F(k,\ell)$ denote the number of linear extensions $L\in\operatorname{\mathcal{E}}(P)$ satisfying $L(y)-L(x)=k$ and $L(z)-L(y)=\ell$. **Brightwell–Felsner–Trotter's cross-product conjecture.** For all $k,\ell\geq 1$,

$$
F(k,\ell)F(k+1,\ell+1)\leq F(k,\ell+1)F(k+1,\ell).
$$

The conjecture was open in general when formulated, but this paper proves it for all posets of width two; the general case remains unresolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09009

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).
source_name: Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak and Greta Panova, “The cross-product conjecture for width two posets”, arXiv:2104.09009 (2022).
